<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|334|THE ACTES|CHA. XV.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=15|verse=3}}† They therfore being brought on their vvay by the Church, passed through Phœnîce and Samaria, reporting the conuersion of the Gentiles: and they made great ioy to al the brethren.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=4}}† And when they were come to Hierusalem, they vvere receiued of the Church and of the Apostles and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Ancients here, & often in this chapter, are the same that Priests vers. 2. as S. Hierom taketh it also ''1. Pet. 5.'' &}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''πρεσβυτέρων''}}∷ Auncients, declaring vvhatsoeuer God had done vvith them. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=5}}† And there arose certaine of the heresie of the Pharisees that beleeued, saying, That they must be circumcised, commaunded also to keepe the lavv of Moyses. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=6}}† And the {{sup|‖}} Apostles and Auncients {{sup|‖}} assembled to consider of this vvord.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=7}}† And vvhen there vvas made a {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 10, 20.''}}* great disputation, {{sup|‖}} Peter rising vp said to them, Men brethren, you knovv that {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annot. vers. 28 toward the ende. · Act. 10, 20.}}∷ of old daies God among vs {{sup|‖}} chose, that by my mouth the Gentiles should heare the vvord of the Gospel, and beleeue. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=8}}† And God vvhich knovveth the hartes, gaue testimonie, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 10, 45.''}}* giuing vnto them the holy Ghost as vvel as to vs, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=9}}† and hath put no difference betvvene vs and them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ By that faith which worketh by charitie. for a dead faith can not purifie the hart of man. See chap. ''16, 31''.}}∷ by faith purifying their hartes. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=10}}† Novv therfore vvhy tempt you God, to put a yoke vpon the neckes of the disciples, vvhich neither our fathers nor vve haue been able to beare? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=11}}† but by the grace of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} vve beleeue to be saued, in like maner as they also.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=12}}† And al the multitude held their peace: and they heard Barnabas and Paul telling vvhat great signes and vvonders God had done among the Gentiles by them.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=13}}† And after they held their peace, {{sup|‖}} Iames answered, saying, Men brethren, heare me. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=14}}† Simon hath told hovv God first visited to take of the Gentiles a people to his name. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=15}}† And to this accord the vvordes of the prophets, as it is vvritten: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=16}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Tim. 3, 5.''}}* ''After these things I vvil returne, and vvil reedifie the tabernacle of Dauid, which was fallen, and the ruines thereof I vvil reedifie, and set it vp'': {{verse|chapter=15|verse=17}}† ''that the residue of men may seeke after the Lord, and al nations vpon whom my name is inuocated, saith the Lord that doeth these things''. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=18}}† To our Lord vvas his ovvne vvorke knovven from the beginning of the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=19}}† For the vvhich cause I iudge, that they vvhich of the Gentiles are conuerted to God, are not to be disquieted, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=20}}† but to write vnto them that they refraine them selues from the contaminations of Idols, and fornication, and strangled things, and bloud. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=21}}† For Moyses of old times hath in euery citie them that preach him in the synagogs, vvhere he is read euery Sabboth.<noinclude>{{rh|||Then}}</noinclude>
